newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: First BCCI payments to depositors seen by year-end.
newsitem.headline: First BCCI payments to depositors seen by year-end.

text.p: Liquidators for the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (Overseas) said they planned to make the first payment to depositors and creditors of the bank before the end of the year.

Ian Wight, the BCCI liquidator, said in a statement issued late Wednesday that the first payments of of about $0.24 on the dollar would be made before 1997. The payment was approved earlier this month by a Luxembourg court which supervises two BCCI entities.

After the first 24 percent of each claim is paid, a remaining payment of between 10 and 15 percent of a creditor's claim will be paid at some point in the future, the statement said. "When we first began the job, we feared that creditors would lose everything. The fact that creditors will now receive a quarter of their money back, with further dividends to come, is encouraging," Wight said.

BCCI banking offices around the world were closed in 1991 by various government agencies after the Bank of England found evidence of massive fraud on a global basis. The BCCI collapse eventually amounted to an estimated US$10 billion loss to depositors and creditors, the biggest banking failure in history.
